who: Jeff A. Webb, historian of Newfoundland at Memorial University, PhD University of New Brunswick.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Jeff A. Webb (Jeffrey Allison) as the author of The Voice of Newfoundland (2008).
Identifies Jeff Webb as a Memorial history professor and author of The Voice of Newfoundland and Observing the Outports.
February 24, 2000 university Gazette says Jeff Webb earned his PhD at UNB and had taught at Memorial for eight years.
Spring 2012 contributor statement identifies Jeff A. Webb as a historian teaching at Memorial University.

notes: Name, distinctive book, institution and doctoral institution agree. The 1994 doctorate year was not independently verified.

who: John Hubbel Weiss, historian of modern Europe at Cornell University, PhD Harvard 1977.

evidence.says: Authority identifies John Hubbel Weiss as author of The Making of Technological Man (1982).
Publisher identifies the book author John Hubbel Weiss as an assistant professor of history at Cornell.
Scholarly review identifies this book as the published version of a Harvard PhD thesis defended in 1977.
Cornell announces John Weiss’s retirement in May 2019 and describes his teaching in twentieth-century European political history.
A 2006 author statement identifies a John Weiss as an emeritus history professor at Lehman College and the CUNY Graduate Center.

notes: The candidate matches the Cornell supervisor and Harvard 1977 doctorate. The CUNY student may reflect a conflation with the CUNY historian John Weiss; that student’s attribution to this candidate is unverified.

who: Gregory S. Wilson, modern US historian at the University of Akron, PhD Ohio State 2001.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Gregory S. Wilson as author of Communities Left Behind (2009).

Institutional CV records Akron appointments from 2001, a modern US history PhD at Ohio State in 2001, and Communities Left Behind. It names Thomas Weyant (2016), Christa Adams (2015) and Matthew Hiner (2006) as dissertations he directed.

notes: The CV directly confirms all three listed students, in addition to the degree, institution and authority-linked book.

who: Major L. Wilson, history professor at Memphis State University/University of Memphis, PhD Kansas 1964.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Major L. Wilson as author of The Presidency of Martin Van Buren (1984).

University retirees’ newsletter, p. 26, records his Kansas history PhD in 1964, Memphis State history appointment from 1965 to retirement in 1995, mentoring three PhD candidates, and authorship of The Presidency of Martin Van Buren.

notes: Exact doctorate and faculty period agree; the same book connects the faculty member to the authority record.

who: Cindy Sondik Aron, historian of American women at the University of Virginia, PhD Maryland 1981.

evidence.says: Authority links Cindy Sondik Aron and Cindy S. Aron to Ladies and Gentlemen of the Civil Service and the 1981 work To Barter Their Souls for Gold.
Department identifies Cindy S. Aron as professor emerita specializing in American women’s history, with Maryland PhD 1981; lists both authority-linked works.
1987 AHA program identifies Cindy Sondik Aron at the University of Virginia as author of Ladies and Gentlemen of the Civil Service.

notes: Full and abbreviated names, institution, doctorate and publications agree.

who: Jay W. Baird, history professor at Miami University, Ohio, appointed 1967; PhD Columbia 1966.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Jay W. Baird as author of To Die for Germany and Hitler’s War Poets.

Miami’s 2004–2006 bulletin lists Jay W. Baird, appointed 1967, as professor of history, with Columbia MA 1960 and PhD 1966. The bulletin explains that the parenthesized year marks employment commencement.

notes: Name, history department, appointment period and doctorate agree. LC authority was retrieved; the Wikidata item was not accessible.

who: Bert Jude (B. J.) Barickman, historian of Brazil and associate professor at the University of Arizona.

evidence.says: Authority explicitly expands B. J. Barickman to Bert Jude Barickman and identifies A Bahian Counterpoint (1998).
Arizona’s history department identifies Bert Barickman as an associate professor in its In Memoriam faculty listing.
Publisher identifies B. J. Barickman as an associate professor of Latin American history at Arizona and author of A Bahian Counterpoint.
Publisher-supplied 1998 book information identifies author Bert Jude Barickman/B. J. Barickman as assistant professor of history at Arizona.

notes: Full name, initials, book and faculty institution agree. The Illinois 1990 doctorate was not independently verified.

who: Lydia Barnett, historian of science and the environment at Northwestern University, PhD Stanford 2011.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Lydia Barnett as author of After the Flood (2019).
Department identifies Lydia Barnett as associate professor, Stanford PhD 2011, and author of After the Flood; she joined Northwestern in 2015.
Institutional CV records a Northwestern history appointment from 2015 and a Stanford history PhD completed in 2011.

notes: Name, book, exact doctorate and Northwestern employment throughout the listed students’ completion years agree.
